title: Rippers Unmasked — 1892 Calendaria
description: Drives Calendaria's world clock to the exact 1892 Almanack: the Gregorian year starting Friday 1 January 1892 (leap), an Earth moon whose 49 quarter-phases — including all 12 mechanically-live full moons — land on their real historical dates via Calendaria's anchorPhases config, and all 60 campaign events seeded as GM notes. Foundry VTT v13. Integrates against Calendaria release-1.0.17 (the last v13-compatible build — install 1.0.17 specifically, NOT latest). Original campaign content; a personal-table module, not for redistribution.

requires.reason: Hosts the world clock, moon, and notes. Pin release-1.0.17 — the last Foundry-v13-compatible Calendaria (1.1.0+ are v14-only). The 1892 moon uses Calendaria's phaseMode:'fixed' + anchorPhases, present in 1.0.17.

rippers-calendaria.note: v0.1.2: event seeding uses its OWN world flag (eventsSeeded), separate from the calendar/date/almanac flag — so a world that ran v0.1.0 (which threw on the calendarnote subtype and left events unseeded) now re-seeds events on update+reload WITHOUT resetting the clock. The events-fallback and almanac journal creation are idempotent (skip if one already exists), so no duplicates. --- v0.1.1: event seeding is now RESILIENT — it seeds native Calendaria calendar notes only when the calendaria.calendarnote JournalEntryPage subtype is a registered valid type (game.documentTypes), and otherwise (or on any per-note failure) lands the events as pages in a plain GM "1892 Events" journal so they never throw the "not a valid type for the JournalEntryPage" validation error seen when Calendaria is not the pinned 1.0.17 build on v13. Moon/calendar registration unchanged. --- Runtime integration only — no packs. On Calendaria's `calendaria.ready` hook this module derives a `rippers-1892` calendar from Calendaria's live `gregorian` (splicing in an Earth moon with a 49-entry anchorPhases table generated from lodge-docs/almanack-1892-data by tools/build-calendaria.mjs), registers it via CALENDARIA.api.addCalendar, persists it into Calendaria's customCalendars setting, and on first run (GM) sets it active, sets the date to 1 Jan 1892, seeds 60 GM notes, and builds a GM almanac journal. All 12 full moons land on their exact real dates via #findExactAnchor. No monkey-patching, no v12-removed hooks. Clearing the world flag rippers-calendaria.setupComplete re-runs first-run setup.
